raw_response:
I have farmed in Mtwara for many years, and I know this soil. At sixty-seven, I do not have money to waste on chemical fertilizer or hybrid seeds from town, so I will spread manure from our goats and plant the maize seed we kept from last season, intercropped with beans as always. We depend on the rains here, so there is no need for irrigation, and I do not trust those chemicals—I would rather have my family pull the weeds by hand. My children and grandchildren will do most of the work on this plot, but I will pay two young men for five days to help with the first clearing because my back is not strong like it used to be.
